conventions.convention: The contrastive score is f(x)ᵀ(f(x−)−f(x+)); the source losses are hinge (1+t)+ and base-2 logistic log₂(1+eᵗ), both equal to one at zero.
Positive examples are independent conditional on their shared class; the negative has a fresh independent class. Binary tasks condition on distinct ordered classes and use uniform labels.
The vector Rademacher complexity uses independent coordinate signs, a one-sided supremum without absolute value, and no 1/M normalization.
Collision probability τ is less than one. For τ>0, s(f) averages under the collision-conditioned class law ν; for τ=0, s(f)=0 and the total contrastive risk equals the distinct-class risk.
L_sup averages the taskwise infimum over linear weights. The mean weight is μ_C+−μ_C−. Risk and supremum measurability are assumed, and measurable empirical selectors are separately assumed to exist.
Uniform generalization assumes AC, R>0, M≥1 and 0<δ<1; Γ uses the loss oscillation B, the coefficient 2√18 L₀R/M, and log(4/δ).
The sub-Gaussian margin comparison uses hinge loss only, allows σ²=0, and uses separate γ formulas for R≥1 and 0<R<1, with 0<ε≤1.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the measurable one-negative latent-class model, nonempty class of measurable representations bounded by R>0 in finite dimension, IID triplets, contrastive and binary-task risks, collision-conditioned deviation s(f), measurable suprema, and separately assumed measurable empirical selectors.

Assuming AC and the stated risk, sample, independent-copy and sign-supremum measurability in the one-negative model, for R>0, M≥1 and 0<δ<1, with probability at least 1−δ every f satisfies |L_un(f)−Lhat_un(f)|≤Γ_M(S,δ), where Γ=2√18 L₀R R_S(F)/M+3B_(ℓ,R)√(ln(4/δ)/(2M)).

In the one-negative model, total contrastive risk decomposes into collision and distinct-class risks. For τ>0, 1≤L_un^=(f)≤1+√2 L₀s(f) for every bounded representation and either source loss. For τ=0, L_un=L_un^≠ and s(f)=0.
In the one-negative latent-class model with τ<1, uniform task labels, and either source hinge or logistic loss, every measurable bounded representation satisfies L_sup^μ(f)≤L_un^≠(f).

For m,d≥1, nonempty bounded V⊆(Rᵈ)^m, and functions h_i:Rᵈ→R with common Lipschitz constant L≥0, E sup_v Σ_i ε_i h_i(v_i)≤√3 L E sup_v Σ_i,t η_it v_it. Both suprema are one-sided; h_i(0)=0 is unnecessary, and V may be infinite.

Under AC and the uniform-generalization hypotheses, a measurable selector in F satisfying the empirical η-minimizer condition almost surely obeys L_un(fhat)≤L_un(f)+2Γ_M(S,δ)+η simultaneously for every comparator f with probability at least 1−δ.

In the one-negative model with hinge loss, a representation bounded by R>0 whose centered classwise vectors have common directional sub-Gaussian proxy σ²≥0 satisfies L_un^≠(f)≤γ L_(γ,sup)^μ(f)+ε for 0<ε≤1, with γ=1+2Rσ√(2ln R+ln(3/ε)) when R≥1 and γ=1+2Rσ√ln(3/ε) when R<1.

Natural logarithm convention and inverse-exponential identities.
Exponential definition and the positive-series estimate in the logistic counterexample.
Differentiating the logistic loss twice.
Converting the logistic derivative bound into a global Lipschitz bound.

Logarithm monotonicity, positivity of ln 2, and logarithmic tail calculations.

Expectation as integration; finite-dimensional expectations are explicitly entrywise.
Mutual independence and common-law conventions for sampled triplets.
Coordinatewise covariance and centered second moments.

Probability-law normalization and countable additivity.
Product laws of independent samples and factorization of cross moments and moment-generating functions.

Iterated integration of bounded functions under probability product laws.
Mean-classifier comparison, collision-loss lower bound, and the first-moment/second-moment inequality.

concerns.concern: The Statement describes L_sup as 'the infimum of the average binary-task risk over all linear classifiers', whereas def-latent-class-contrastive-learning defines the average of the taskwise infima. These orders differ if the former means one common weight across tasks. The proof and F1 use the definition's taskwise convention correctly; align this explanatory wording with that definition.

The source metadata locator says '§4 default setting, printed p. 6; §4.2 and Figure 8, printed p. 8', and F1 attributes the default configuration to Section 4. In the linked [SimCLR paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/chen20j/chen20j.pdf), the default-setting paragraph is in §2.3 on PDF page 3, and §4.2/Figure 8 is on PDF page 6. The reported configuration and performance comparisons themselves match the source.

The reference label '[Lei et al., Lemma A.1, complete vector-contraction proof]' overstates that locator. [Lei et al., Appendix A](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.12383), PDF page 14, states Lemma A.1 with attribution to Maurer and then proceeds to the proof of Lemma 4.3; it does not give a proof of Lemma A.1 there. The local √3 proof is self-contained, and the accompanying description as a contrastive-learning application is accurate.

seams_checked.note: Opened def-rademacher-complexity and thm-rademacher-uniform-generalization. The consumer explicitly converts the normalized one-sided scalar convention to its unnormalized vector convention. It shifts and scales the loss into [0,1], carries AC and the relevant measurability assumptions, uses the supplier's two-sided empirical bound with log(4/δ), and multiplies back by the oscillation B. The supplier statement supports exactly this application; neither direction reveals a normalization or hypothesis mismatch.
